title: There is thought and there is thought: the hidden thought of will and the analytical thought of bina
overview:
Chapter 40 begins the root of the letters of thought of *bina*. The *Zohar* says "there is thought and there is thought": a thought of will and a thought of intellect. The will dresses at once in thought, so the two are one; because the will is hidden, its thought is the hidden thought, and above it is the *machshava kduma*, the primal thought.

The talk after the first class, running over two more tapes, stays there: the *igulim* are the primal desires a person is born with, like a baby who will want a car, and no *mashal* can show them; the explanations are pointers, and one has to follow the garments of thought inward, like seeing a ninja by his suit.

The will goes into the nerves without letters, yet moves the hand exactly. The other thought is *machshava iyunis*, analysis, which tries a *sevara* and discards it, as in the Talmud and the scientific method, and comes from *Malchus* of *tevuna* into the letters of *Leah*. Both are rooted in the essence of the soul, and the will leads the intellect: a person thinks about what he wants.

sections.title: There is thought and there is thought: the will is called thought
sections.summary: The chapter turns to the root of the letters of thought of *bina*. There are two kinds of thought, a thought of wanting and a thought of thinking something out; the will dresses at once in thought, so the two are one and each is called by the other's name, and because the will is hidden, its thought is called the hidden thought.

phrases.he: (מ) ומעתה יש להבין דרך פרט בבחינת שרש אותיות המחשבה דבינה ותבונה ולאה כו’ בהיות מבואר בזהר בכמה דוכתי
דאית מחשבה ואית מחשבה כו'
phrases.en: There is a *machshava* and there's a *machshava*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת מחשבה סתימאה דאריך אנפין ומחשבה הקדומה דאדם קדמון וכהאי גוונא והענין הוא דהרצון נקרא גם כן בשם מחשבה בלשון הקודש

blocks.text: **There is a *machshava* and there's a *machshava***: the *Zohar*'s two kinds of thought. One is a thought of *ratzon* (will), of wanting something. The other is a thought of *bina* (understanding): analysis, thinking something out, the thought of the intellect.

phrases.he: כמו כאשר חשב, כאשר רצה כידוע
phrases.en: Like it says by Haman: what he wanted to do.

phrases.he: כי הרצון מלובש מיד במחשבה שבמוח,
phrases.en: The *ratzon* immediately gets enclothed in *machshava*,

phrases.he: על כן הרצון והמחשבה של הרצון אחד הוא,
phrases.en: that's why the *ratzon* and the *machshava* of the *ratzon* is like one thing.

phrases.he: ונקרא המחשבה בשם רצון והרצון בשם מחשבה
כמו כאשר עלה ברצונו,
היינו כשעלה במחשבתו כו'
phrases.en: Came out in his thought.

blocks.text: The will is called thought too. The verse says of Haman *kaasher chashav*, "as he thought", and it means what he wanted to do. **The *ratzon* immediately gets enclothed in *machshava***, so the will and the thought of the will are one thing, and each is called by the other's name: "it came up in his will" means it **came out in his thought**, and *kach ala b'machshava* ("so it came up in thought") is what came out in will.

phrases.he: ונקרא מחשבה סתימאה
phrases.en: And this is called the closed *machshava*.

phrases.he: על שם בחינת ההעלם של הרצון, על כן המחשבה שבו הרצון הוא גם כן בהעלם וסתימות, ונקרא מחשבה סתימאה
(והוא בחינת אותיות הרצון הנזכר לעיל)
phrases.en: The letters of the *ratzon*.

blocks.text: It is called *machshava stima'a*, **the closed *machshava***, because the will is hidden, and so the thought the will is in is hidden and closed as well. These are the letters of the will: the letters that say what the will is.

sections.title: The primal thought: the will before every will, and how to see it
sections.summary: Higher than the hidden will is the *machshava kduma*, the primal thought, its source; it too is a thought, because it is a will, and so on up to the simple will in the Essence. The talk after class stays on it: the *igulim*, the primal desires a person is born with, which no *mashal* can show and which one has to find in oneself, following the garments of thought inward.

phrases.he: אך הנה בחינת מחשבה הקדומה הוא מקדם לרצון הנעלם,
phrases.en: It's even before the *ratzon hane'elam*,

phrases.he: והוא המקור לרצון הנעלם שנקרא רצון לרצון כו',
וגם זה בחינת מחשבה הוא,
phrases.en: but this is also a *machshava*,

phrases.he: שמלובש בו הרצון הקדום
phrases.en: and this *ratzon hakadum*, since it's a *ratzon*, it's also *meluvash* in *machshava*.

phrases.he: שקדם לכל רצון לרצון (כמו שכתוב באות י"ז)
אבל נקרא בשם מחשבה הקדומה
phrases.en: Called *machshava kduma*.

blocks.text: Higher still is the *machshava kduma* (the primal thought). It is even more hidden: it comes before the hidden will, the *ratzon l'ratzon* (the will for a will) of *Adam Kadmon*, and is its source. Yet the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) in it, being a will, is also dressed in thought, and that is why in some places it is called the *machshava kduma*. A will, on any level, is also called a thought.

After the class a student asks how the whole chain fits, since different places put it differently. *Adam Kadmon* comes in *igulim* (circles) and *yosher* (straightness), and the *igulim* come first. They are part of the *machshava kduma* itself, though *Adam Kadmon* as a whole is also the *machshava kduma*. The difference: the *igulim* are not a will for a will but the *etzem haratzon* (the essence of the will) of the *machshava kduma*.

blocks.title: The will for honor
blocks.text: *Yosher* is a will for a will: he is willing to take up another will in order to get the will he has, like the dog inside a three-sided fence. Take the *midda* of *hod*, or *kavod* (honor). His essential will for honor is the *igul* of *hod* of the *machshava kduma*, *hod* of *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, and as an *igul* it has no form to it at all. What comes out of its *Malchus* is the *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*: now that he wants honor, what is he going to do about it? Something more particular. He will go and make a lot of money, and that will get him honor.

That is why the *Adam Kadmon* of *yosher* is not called will anymore but *chachma*: it has to be a *tzimtzum* (contraction) of the will. He has to think it over and say, "To really get what I want, I have to do this thing that I don't want." That is a will for a will. And why is one needed at all? Because the will it serves was not there before. It is a creation.

blocks.question: Then are the igulim not really circles but nekudim, points?
blocks.text: No, the *nekudim* come after *Adam Kadmon* altogether, in *Arich*: the same kind of thing repeated on a lower level. This is the actual essential will: not a point of will but the essence of the point, and a circle because it is the essence of the will that encompasses everything. The *reshimu* (the impression left after the *tzimtzum*) is called a point because it is not a *makif* (an encompassing light): it has nothing to do with anything, totally inside itself. The *machshava kduma* encompasses everything, everything is included in these *igulim*, and each *igul* is included in the one before it.

blocks.question: Later, on the nekudim, he says the etzem haratzon means the revealed will in its first coming out. Is the essence not sometimes called a point?
blocks.text: It can be called a point, but it is not the *nekudim* where a *partzuf* (a stature) of *nekudim* comes later. What is spoken of here is not only the essence of the revealed will but the actual essential will itself, much, much higher than that.

blocks.title: The politician who wants honor
blocks.text: How can the essential will for honor come after anything? Look at a politician. He wants honor, so he has to do all kinds of things, like giving other people honor. But the essential will for honor is for himself to get honor, and just stomp on everybody. That is in the *igulim*: there is no giving anyone else honor there, because there is nobody else.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at politicians as a type: they want honor for themselves and to "stomp on everybody".
sensitivity.publishable: How can the essential will for honor come after anything? Look at a person who wants honor. He has to do all kinds of things, like giving other people honor. But the essential will for honor is for himself to get honor, and nobody else. That is in the *igulim*: there is no giving anyone else honor there, because there is nobody else.

blocks.question: How is the igul of hod an inner circle of netzach?
blocks.text: Because the *igulim* are one inside the other: he is totally turned inward, inside his whole original *ratzon kadum*. Inside a will for a car is a will for the intellect; really not a will for an intellect but a will to be wise. That is why it gets confused with the *nekudim*: the example given for it is really an example of something later. No example can be given of the *ratzon hastum* (the closed will). The book uses the same example as for *Arich*, the *shochad* (bribe), because all wills work the same way; but remember it is an example. The *ratzon kadum* itself is a will to be wise.

Every will, on its own, is a *ratzon kadum*. The book speaks of a will to have a building, already a particular will; for the *Aibershter* (G-d), too, the *ratzon kadum* for the whole world is like a particular will. See how such a will comes out in revelation and it is for an infinite building; still, that is not its essence. The essence is his own *machshava kduma*: not even him sitting in the building, not for anything. It is simply part of a person that there is a hidden will in him, called *Atika Stima'a* (the hidden Ancient One).

blocks.title: A home, by a man and by a squirrel
blocks.text: It is a hidden will that comes with a person when he is born, right there; really part of the essence, the *tzimtzum* of the *glif glifu* (the engraving), the letters of it that are left. It is what a person wants the way a squirrel comes wanting a hole in a tree. The revealed will is the *nekudim*; before them come the *igulim*, included in the hidden will. And the hidden will does not come as an open thought: an open thought is already the revealed will. It is part of his nature.

blocks.title: The baby and the car
blocks.text: From the minute a baby is born you know that when he grows up he is going to want a car. How? He doesn't know what a car is, not even a toy car; a five-year-old knows that when he is big like papa he'll have his own car, but the baby has no thought of a car at all. Still, there is a hidden thought there: just being a boy, he is going to want a car. It is included.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: So the *igulim* are not even the self-perception; that is already *Adam Kadmon*, a will for a will. The *igulim* are the self, higher than the self-perception, which is already in terms of the worlds. In the *machshava kduma* there is no real *tzimtzum* in the will: the will did not become less than it was. The *tzimtzum* was in the light. The light of the *Atzmus* (G-d's essence), which before was part and parcel of it, withdrew, and now there is just a will.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.question: Is the machshava kduma the letters of the reshimu, as was once explained?
blocks.text: The *reshimu* is the letters of the *glif glifu* as *levushim* (garments) instead of *kelim* (vessels); the *glif glifu* are the *kelim*, part and parcel of the light. The *machshava kduma* is already like a stamp. It is called *Atik*, *Atika d'chol Atikin*, the original *Atik*: a perfect copy of what was in the *reshimu*, not the *reshimu* itself, whose letters are still the letters of the *glif glifu* with the light removed. A copy, but *mamash* (actually) the same thing. And it is not observable: that is why it is called *stima*, hidden.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: Between *tehiru ila'a* and *tehiru tata'a* (the upper and the lower purity) there is a big difference, even though the letters of the will in the *glif glifu* and in the *machshava kduma* are the same letters. *Tehiru ila'a* is how this baby was before he was even conceived: there was no baby at all.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: An agent sells the baby a house
blocks.text: Once he is born, you see little desires, among them a desire for a house: he will want a place to live. If an agent walked up now and said, "I've got a house for you, start saving up," you couldn't talk to him about a house; there is no revealed thought yet. But the *machshava stima'a* is there, built in, because it came right through the *tzimtzum*: the essence of what came into him, now in the *mahus* (nature) of after the *tzimtzum*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.question: Chapter 10 speaks of an actual movement from before the tzimtzum to after it. Is that not only by us?
blocks.text: For us there is a difference between before we were born and after. And there is a difference here too: before, it was the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light); afterwards it is the beginning and birth of *Adam Kadmon*, a person, not the *Aibershter* anymore. But the letters of the will before and after are the same exact letters, by the *glif glifu*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: This is not a matter of explanation but of the *ma'amik* (delving): realize that the explanation is a *mashal* for something much higher, and try to see that level in yourself. You will feel that all your external desires existed before in a *hiyuli* (raw potential) way: not in the essence of the soul but in the essence of the desires themselves, already a *klal*, a whole that includes everything you will ever want. The explanation of *bina* can't give you this; you have to think about it. That is *amkus hadaas* (depth of *daas*), and that is what to do in *davenen* (prayer).
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: Even the *mashal* given on it is really *nekudim*: it is already a revealed thought. No *mashal* can be given on a *machshava stima'a*, because it is hidden, not revealed at all. So you have to see where it is inside you.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: There is a level inside you that is all the *igulim*: all your zeros are there as the primal desires. A child is born with a primal desire for honor, a primal desire for love and a primal desire for *din* (judgement). They are not yet a self-image, because a self-image is already a will for a will: an image of how he will look to others, or even to himself, which is already in a way outside himself. That is why *Adam Kadmon*, compared with the *machshava kduma*, is called a new creation, *Adam d'Beriya*, part of the outside world, the level of thought.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: The *machshava kduma* is still *Atzilus*, which among the general worlds is still part of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite): the *kelim*, the body of the King. There is an eye and a brain up there, but it is the *Adam* of the *igulim*, all still inside Himself with no outside modifications, and so the *igulim* are one inside the other. These are the primal desires; a *ratzon kadum* means a primal desire, the soul that enters the body, not the *yechida*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.question: Why must a primal desire for chesed come before a primal desire for gevura, in the next igul?
blocks.text: Because if you don't love anything, you're not going to hate anything. *Chesed* is what causes the next *igul*: the *gevura* is what He will hate, and what *dinim* and *tzimtzumim* He has to make, according to what He loves. Like a *beis din* (a court): if you don't know what you love, you can't open courts, because courts enforce the society you want, where your kids, whom you love, can be safe in the street. The same with *netzach* and *hod*. But they are one inside the other: He does not yet come out with an actual love. Inside Himself He has a primal desire to be loved and to love, not yet applied to anything. It comes automatically, like what a child is born with.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: The *meshalim* go different ways. In the usual one, the first thought of a particular thought stands for it: for the *Aibershter* it is a particular thought, but for a world it is the primal thought that includes the whole world, and so a particular thought becomes primal for all that is inside it. That is in terms of wills. In terms of persons, *Adam Kadmon* already has a form, like *Adam d'Beriya*; the *machshava kduma* is how it is before the creation, as it comes into *Atzilus* straight out of the *Atzmus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: A house in the Los Angeles area
blocks.text: Each level relates to those above and below it, a *mashal* on a *mashal*, and the first thought of a particular thought is not really the first. When you just bought a house and started thinking about it, that was not the *machshava kduma*: the minute you thought about it, you were already thinking about a house in the Los Angeles area. Trace it back, and the first thought was already included in the essence when it came into the body.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: A place to live, then? A shelter, a home? Not even that: a newborn doesn't know from homes, and yet it is there, hidden, and not even for shelter. Say it is for safety, for this, for that; finally you have to say it is the basic first ten *sefiros* coming out, in a *golem* (an unformed mass).
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: The baby who moves his foot
blocks.text: He is not a person yet. A little child doesn't know where his hands are or how the body works: he means to move his hand and moves his foot, and when he tries to move, he moves everything. He has not become a *partzuf* of a person, separated out into *yosher*; he knows only how it feels inside him, not how it relates to the outside world. The *machshava kduma* is already there; his self-perception in terms of the world is not. That develops, as a will for a will, from what he perceives outside.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: A will for a will comes up only when a person perceives from outside that things are not as they are inside. So how could anything block what the *Aibershter* wants? But the *Aibershter* makes the outside too, and with Him it is the other way around. No outside forced Him to adjust; He wanted an outside, so He made His *hishtalshelus* (chain of descent) go through a will for a will. A will for a will means adjusting yourself from the way you originally are: a new creation, a will that was not there before. The outside comes not from the direct will but from a will for a will, and that is what makes it outside. So even the *mashal* has to be seen in perspective: by us the will for a will comes from the outside; by the *Aibershter* the outside comes from the will for a will.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: Where are the paper cups?
blocks.text: Go back to chapter 1: the main thing is *hisbonenus* (contemplation), and it needs a vessel, *amkus hadaas*. In *Chassidus* there is a part you understand and a part you don't; in fact a part that is not understandable at all. The explanations of *bina* are pointers: they point you to look over there. Ask your mother where the paper cups are. "The second cabinet to the right." "I'm looking, I don't see it." "Look behind the other thing." The final thing is not the explanation: it is that when you follow it, you see it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: This is the difference between the real approach he explains in this book and the mistake of the world: they take the abstract explanation as an abstract thing of its own, and that is why they were never able to get some of the *inyanim* (matters) in this book. It is pointing you to look at certain levels, like the *koach hatnua* (the power of movement) in a living thing. When it says *bina* is like a river, that is a nice image, but more than an image: you actually have a river of *bina* inside you, and you can see it. Where? Follow the book: the spring of *bina* goes into *Leah*. Look at your thought, and you'll see that it is always flowing like a river.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.text: From there you can follow it to the flash of *chachma*, even to the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight). *Chassidus* says in various places that you can't see the *koach hamaskil*; that means you can't see it itself. You can see it like a ninja inside his *levushim*: when you see how the garments move, you are seeing the body that moves them. The only thing you can feel and hold on to is the thought, and in it are garments on garments: the garment of *Leah* on the thought that is the *kelim*, on the thought of *Malchus* of *tevuna*, on the thought of *bina*, on the thought of *chachma*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: The ninja
blocks.text: When a man in a shirt and gloves moves, you know exactly where his hand is. A ninja is running around. "I can't see him!" "Shoot the bastard. What do you mean you can't see him? You see those black clothes moving around: shoot at those." You don't have to see his body; shoot at the clothes and you hit the man. Not "Oh man, I killed a ninja suit": the suit is fine, it's the ninja himself. You can even tell his arm from his head, and whether he is fat or skinny, because a ninja wears a close-fitting suit, like a stocking, not a tent. So with the letters: the external letters are the exact shape of the internal letters, fitted like a bodysuit.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: The clothes show the man
blocks.text: From the clothing of a king you can see not just the body but the soul; and not only by a king. See how a person is dressed and you get a look into him, because he dresses according to his thought. Besides the clothes following the outer vessels of his body (a fat guy can't wear a skinny suit), what kind of clothing is it? A tuxedo or jeans? From it you can see the emotions and the intellect, almost whether he is a smart guy or a stupid guy, and *mamash* the will.

sensitivity.publishable: From the clothing of a king you can see not just the body but the soul; and not only by a king. See how a person is dressed and you get a look into him, because he dresses according to his thought. Besides the clothes following the outer vessels of his body (a fat guy can't wear a skinny suit), what kind of clothing is it? A tuxedo or jeans? From it you can see the emotions and the intellect, almost how smart he is, and *mamash* the will.

blocks.text: So with these ideas: what we get are garments of garments, the outer clothes and under them a first and a second set of underwear. Especially in the weather here, two degrees last night with a windchill of fifteen below: for sure he's wearing a few sets.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: Find the ten bunnies
blocks.text: This is what it means that *Moshiach* will teach by way of *re'iya* (sight): he will point to it. People think he'll come and make a magic on you and all of a sudden you'll see, as with Elisha or Yeshayahu, he is not sure which, who did something and a man suddenly saw angels all over. That is not what it is talking about. He will tell you what things are, and you'll say, "That's right, there it is." Like the ten hidden bunnies in the picture: "Look on the tree, on the side there; see those two leaves?" Up to then it is all explanations, but the explanations are not just explanations.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 211 reads no line: it is the rest of the talk with a student that began after class 210 read line 9, on the machshava kduma of this line.

blocks.title: When to do the hisbonenus
blocks.text: These are abstractions, explanations of where to look, and where to look is *mibsari echeze Eloka* ("from my flesh I see G-d"). Someone once asked the Rebbe that it is hard to figure out which *hisbonenus* to do where in *davenen*. The Rebbe said to leave that to the people of the past generations: you can do the *hisbonenus* separately, before or after *davenen*; just sit and think it. The best time is maybe at *davenen*, or another time when you have time to sit and think.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

sensitivity.reason: Practical guidance on prayer, retold from the Rebbe without a source, that a reader could act on.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether a secondhand report of the Rebbe's advice on where hisbonenus belongs relative to davenen should print as told.
sensitivity.publishable: These are abstractions, explanations of where to look, and where to look is *mibsari echeze Eloka* ("from my flesh I see G-d"). The best time for the *hisbonenus* is maybe at *davenen*, or another time when you have time to sit and think.

blocks.text: The book explains how the will, *chachma*, *bina* and thought work, and when it says a person wants a house, it is talking about you, when you want something: a will for honor, or a physical desire, an ice cream. Most people look at a will as a thing up there: *Atik* and *Arich*, will and delight, deep Kabbalistic things; the Arizal maybe knows what a will is. No: it means when you want a piece of pizza. Take a look at that, with its emotions and intellect, and analyze it in terms of this *hisbonenus*. That is *tevuna*: taking it in terms of actuality, not just understanding explanations you never brought down to anything. Take the intellect you are actually having, and follow it back to the *koach hamaskil*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.title: Pants on the floor
blocks.text: You won't see the *koach hamaskil* itself, but you'll see it as clearly as what is revealed of it. You can see your letters of thought, and that they are moving: something inside is moving them. A pair of pants can lie on the floor, or have somebody inside. Look at the garment of thought and you'll see there is something moving it. You can't see the *koach hamaskil* naked, but you can see it dressed, moving things.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.text: The rest you can literally feel in your body and emotions. When something excites you, your lungs start, the *hevel halev* (breath of the heart): that is your emotions, the outer vessels of *Zeir Anpin* in the *olam katan* (the small world, man). Know how it is in the small world and you know how it is upstairs, world after world, from the general of the general down to the small world. Look at how it is there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.title: The Super Bowl on television
blocks.text: It is like watching a football game on television. Today was the Super Bowl, and a lot of people say they saw the game. You didn't see the game; you were looking at a television, with teeny little guys running on the screen. Yet they saw exactly the whole game, because it is a small world: a copy of a copy of a copy, from the camera to a station to another, until it reaches your screen. So the book tells you where to look and what to see: when it moves like this, that is what it means, and the thing it moves in is the inner part. That is the *amkus hadaas* of the *hisbonenus*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.text: *Amkus hadaas* means to connect your mind to the actual thing, not a vague concept, so that you can have a *hakara* (recognition) and a *hargesh* (feeling) of it, as *Chassidus* says. *Im ein bina ein daas, im ein daas ein bina* (without understanding there is no knowledge, without knowledge no understanding): without *bina* you don't know where to look; without *daas*, connecting until you recognize what was explained, you will never really understand what it is talking about. When an emotion comes up, the breath of the heart starts, the rhythm gets faster or slower, deeper or harder, the heart beats harder, and there is an inner emotion you feel: that is the actual feeling of what was explained to you.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.text: That is why most of the people who sat and learned *Chassidus* don't understand nothing. They are not stupid people; maybe we are slightly smarter than them, but a lot of them are pretty smart, and in things they feel, like money, they have a big smartness. This they never tried to feel, so they don't understand it.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

sensitivity.reason: Says most people who learned Chassidus understand nothing, and that "we" are slightly smarter than them.
sensitivity.publishable: That is why many of the people who sat and learned *Chassidus* don't understand it. A lot of them are pretty smart, and in things they feel, like money, they have a big smartness. This they never tried to feel, so they don't understand it.

blocks.text: It is *davka* (precisely) the *daas* that gives depth to *bina*: the *ma'amik*, which makes *chachma* and *bina* deeper. It is only a vessel, a matter of *daas* and not of *chachma* and *bina*, yet that is where the real understanding comes from. *Ma'amik* does not mean concentration, clenching your fists real hard and saying, "I still didn't understand." It means to connect to the idea, to feel what the idea is talking about.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.text: When it speaks of intellect and emotions, there is a feeling of what they are. Look at the actual intellect and emotions, *b'poel mamash* (in actual fact), and follow it up. Behind the *bina* there is a source. You can't see it directly; you can't see the *bina* directly either, only the letters of *Leah*. But you see that something is moving them, and something moving that, until you reach the body moving the garments: now you are at the *kelim*. Look further and there is a soul moving the body, and that whole thing is a garment of something higher. That is what *ma'amik* is, the whole matter of *daas*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

blocks.text: Without *daas* there will be no real *bina*: it stays where it is, no *tevuna* comes out of it, and it is never connected to anything. Until you say: what do I need this *Chassidus* for? Will, *Atik*, *Arich*, all high level; can you eat it? You can't do nothing with it. The basic thing is a matter of *re'iya*: you have to actually look at the things it is explaining.
blocks.outOfPlace: Tape 212 reads no line: it continues tape 211's talk on how to see these levels in oneself, which began on this line.

phrases.he: וכך יובן עד רום המעלות,
phrases.en: And this keeps going up and up,

phrases.he: גם במחשבה דרצון הפשוט שבעצמות ממש (הנזכר לעיל באות יו"ד).

blocks.text: **And this keeps going up and up**, even to the thought of the *ratzon hapashut* (the simple will) in the very Essence: to say there is a simple will means a *machshava pshuta*, a simple thought, as in section 10.

sections.title: The will in the nerves: a simple thought without letters
sections.summary: A will that comes suddenly into the brain goes into its nerves as a simple thought, not made of letters: its letters are not vessels but the will itself. Yet the movement it makes is exact, defined all the way down to letters of action.

phrases.he: והנה אנו רואים שהרצון הבא פתאום במוח, הוא בא בגידי המוח במחשבה פשוטה ולא מורכבת מאותיות כלל
כי באמת אין לרצון בחינת כלי כשאר האותיות כמו אור השכל בכלי המוח

blocks.question: He just said the will is called thought and thought is called will, almost interchangeable. Now he says the will comes into the brain without letters. How is that possible?
blocks.text: It means they are not the same kind of thing: these are not really *kelim*. Those letters are the *etzem haratzon*, a simple thought, because the will is still not really outside the *Atzmus*; the will and the *taanug* (delight) are almost part of the *Atzmus*, all the way down to *Atik* and *Arich*. The letters of the will are not like regular letters of thought, a vessel to hold something: they are *mamash* the same thing. That thought is the will.

phrases.he: אך בגידי המוח (שנקרא נערוי"ן הדקין ביותר,
שמהם כח התנועה וכח ההרגש באברים כידוע)
phrases.en: From the nerve comes two powers, the power of movement and the power of feeling.

phrases.he: מתפשט כח ואור הרצון גם להיות האברים נשמעים לרצונו שבמוח
כמו לפשוט ידו ורגלו
phrases.en: like to stretch his hand or his foot,

phrases.he: או לכווצם
רק על פי הרצון שעולה במוח פתאום כידוע.
phrases.en: And the *ratzon* comes in the *moach* out of *pisom*, like instantly, as is known.

blocks.text: The will goes into the *gidei hamoach* (the nerves of the brain), not like letters coming into the intellect. Yet it is not totally without letters: when it does what he wants, the movement is defined. Wanting a piece of bread, he reaches exactly for the bread. It is defined in letters down to letters of *Asiya*, so "without letters" has to be taken the right way.

blocks.title: Chachma with dimensions
blocks.text: A friend once told of learning with a young man who reached the place where it says *chachma* has dimensions. "That can't be true; I heard *chachma* is a point with no dimensions." What do you mean? You're arguing with the *Mitteler Rebbe*? There are places where it says *chachma* has no letters either. But here he says the will has no letters, unlike *chachma*, the light of the intellect in the vessel of the brain. Elsewhere *chachma* is how the thought comes before the letters; so here the letters are not really separate things, vessels.

**From the nerve comes two powers, the power of movement and the power of feeling**. The power of the will spreads to the limb that obeys it, **like to stretch his hand or his foot**: he wants to go somewhere and his feet start walking. The will comes as a simple thought above letters, yet it moves the limb exactly. A person doesn't just sort of move; he knows exactly what he wants and grabs it, all by the will that comes up suddenly. That is one kind of thought, the thought of will.

sections.title: The other thought: analytical thought of bina
sections.summary: The other thought is made of actual letters: *machshava iyunis*, analytical thought, which tries a line of reasoning and discards it, like a proof in the Talmud or the scientific method. It has no will in it, sits in the brain of *bina*, comes from *Malchus* of *tevuna* just above the letters of *Leah*, and is preceded by a take on the matter before any argument.

phrases.he: והנה יש מחשבה אחרת בבחינת אותיות המחשבה ממש
phrases.en: This is *mamash* in the way of *osios hamachshava*, meaning a separate *machshava* of *osios*.

phrases.he: שהוא בא על ידי בחינת בינה והשגה תחלה,
phrases.en: This comes through first of all an explanation and a reach,

phrases.he: שנקרא מחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: *Machshava iyunis* means he takes and he analyzes the thing.

blocks.text: There is another thought, *mamash* letters of thought, **a separate *machshava* of *osios***. In the will, the letters are the will itself. In thought there are various thoughts you think a thing over with, and the basic way a person thinks is that he thinks and then discards: "Is it like this? Nah, it can't be. Maybe like this? Nah." That is logic: you have a *sevara* (a line of reasoning), you think, "So it would have worked like this," and you say, "No, no." So the thought with its letters is not necessarily from the essence of the intellect; it is an external vessel to it, and that is what it means that it actually has letters. The other thought is not a separate thought: the will is the thought and the thought is the will.

**This comes through first of all an explanation and a reach**: the logical. It is called *machshava iyunis*: **he takes and he analyzes the thing**. First he cuts it up into separate parts, then he comes up with *sevaros* and sees whether each one works, as in the Talmud: "So I have a *sevara*." A *sevara* is basically a theory.

What we call *iyun* (analysis) is actually the scientific method. There is really no such thing as science: most who believe in it never learned it. Rabbi Markel did, as a chemistry honors student at McGill. Science does not come up with actual things: it comes only from *Nehi* of *Arich*, not from the inner place, the *mazalos*, and goes only into the world. They come up with a theory and test it.

sensitivity.reason: Says there is no such thing as science and that most who believe in it never learned it.
sensitivity.publishable: What we call *iyun* (analysis) is actually the scientific method. Rabbi Markel learned science, as a chemistry honors student at McGill. Science does not come up with actual things: it comes only from *Nehi* of *Arich*, not from the inner place, the *mazalos*, and goes only into the world. They come up with a theory and test it.

blocks.title: Found money: Eilu Metzios
blocks.text: The Talmud works the same way. Look at what little children start with, *Eilu Metzios*. There are two theories, of Rava and Abaye: one says *yiush shelo midaas* (giving up hope on a lost thing one does not yet know is lost) is a good *yiush*, the other says it is not. Then comes *ta shma*, "come and hear": here is an application. If you find money you may keep it; this proves that *yiush shelo midaas* is a good *yiush*, since maybe the man doesn't know yet that he lost it. The other answers that it proves nothing, because a person always feels his pocket, *mimashmesh*; if he lost money he knows it, so it is a *yiush midaas*. It neither proves nor disproves the *sevara*. Two *sevaros* fight it out, but a person can do the same in his own brain: "That proves it. Oh wait, no, it doesn't."

So he picked up a thought and discarded it. And the thought about money was totally external, nothing to do with the inner intellect of *yiush shelo midaas*: an application, like a test, a scientific test. You take the *sevara* and try it out.

blocks.title: The scientific experiment in Chelm
blocks.text: Like the famous scientific test in Chelm. One says bread always falls on the buttered side, the other says it always falls on the unbuttered side. So they did a scientific experiment: they buttered a piece of bread, it fell, and it fell on the buttered side. "Hey, you buttered it on the wrong side!" This is a *machshava iyunis*.

*Machshava iyunis* can also go, as with the scientific method, on an intellect coming only out of *Nehi* of *Arich*: they just want to find out what's going on in the world, and are not looking into the inner thing. This is called *machshava iyunis*.

phrases.he: כמו שאנו רואים בכל שכל וסברא, שהשכלתו יושג
במוח בינה (בלשון אידיש פאר שטאנד)
phrases.en: in the brain of understanding,

phrases.he: שבא מיד בעיון המחשבה הנקרא מחשבת שכל
phrases.en: That right away will come in *iyun hamachshava*, called *machshevas sechel*.

phrases.he: והוא כח מחשבה עיונית להכיל כל עיון שכלי דוקא,
שאין בו רצון כלל
phrases.en: There's no actual *ratzon* in this.

blocks.text: Every intellect and *sevara* is grasped **in the brain of understanding**, *farshtand* in Yiddish, and right away it comes into all kinds of thoughts: this is the *machshevas sechel* (the thought of the intellect).

In this thought itself **there's no actual *ratzon***; there is a will to understand, but not in the thought. Bringing up the found money, he does not necessarily want to prove it is the way he says. If he did, that would be a will turning the intellect, like a *shochad* (bribe), to prove his point. A real will to understand is open to whatever comes out.
He does the experiment not because he *davka* wants it to come out one way. Not like the scientists who work for a cigarette company and do their experiment to prove that cigarettes are good for you.

sensitivity.reason: A jab at scientists who work for cigarette companies.
sensitivity.publishable: He does the experiment not because he *davka* wants it to come out one way.

blocks.text: A real intellect is not like that. In one place Abaye answers for Rav: he raises a point and answers it against his own position, because he has no will to prove it is like him. There is a will to understand, since the intellect comes out of *Arich*; but the *machshava iyunis* itself is a thought of intellect, not of will.

phrases.he: ולא נקרא מחשבה זו בשם רצון כלל,
phrases.en: It's not a *ratzon*, it's an intellect.

phrases.he: להיותה אינה בגידי המוח כלל,
phrases.en: And it doesn't go into the *gidei hamoach*, it doesn't go into the nerves to do something,

phrases.he: רק במוח הבינה ממש
phrases.en: rather it's actually in the *moach habina*, in the lobes of the brain basically.

phrases.he: דהיינו בכלי ההשגה וההבנה של השכל עצמו, שם יש כלי להמחשבה עיונית לכל השגה שכלית
והוא בחינת מלכות דתבונה,
phrases.en: This *machshava iyunis* comes from *Malchus d'tevuna*,

phrases.he: דהיינו סוף מדריגת אור ההשגה בעצם המביא להשגה בענין הנבדל (הנזכר לעיל באות ב')

blocks.text: This thought is not called will at all: **it's not a *ratzon*, it's an intellect**. It does not go into the nerves to do something; it is in the brain of *bina*, **in the lobes of the brain basically**, in the vessels of grasp and understanding of the intellect itself, where there is a vessel for analytical thought. It comes from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, where the letters come out: the end of the light of comprehension, as in section 2.

phrases.he: משם נעשה כח מחשבת שכל הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: From there comes the *machshevas sechel*, what's called a *machshava iyunis*.

phrases.he: כי תחלה באה אור השגת השכל גם בלא מחשבה עיונית עדיין
phrases.en: It first comes in a way of before the *machshava iyunis*,

phrases.he: (הנקרא דער פאר נעמען אין פאר שטאנד אליין כו')
phrases.en: the actual take that he has on it.

phrases.he: טרם שחושב אור ההשכלה בלבוש דמחשבה ועיון עדיין,
אך מיד מתפשט המושג והמושכל במחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: And immediately it is *nispashet* into *machshava iyunis*.

blocks.text: From *Malchus* of *tevuna* comes the *machshevas sechel*. But first the grasp of the intellect comes without analytical thought, what is called in Yiddish *der farnemen in farshtand*: **the actual take that he has on it**. Before Abaye and Rava argue, each has a take: one sees *yiush shelo midaas* as a *yiush*, the other sees that it is not. That comes even before the *sevara*, the reason why he sees it that way. **And immediately it is *nispashet* into *machshava iyunis***, dressed in the thought of the intellect.

phrases.he: וזהו בחינת מלכות דתבונה
שלמעלה מבחינת אותיות המחשבה שנקרא לאה
phrases.en: just above the actual *osios* of the *machshava*, which is called *Leah*.

phrases.he: (וכידוע בענין דלית רבתי דאחד כו',
שהוא בחינת מלכות דתבונה שמאחוריים דאימא כו',
שמשם שרש התהוות המחשבה באותיות ממש כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
phrases.en: That from *Malchus d'tevuna* is the *shoresh* of the *machshava* coming into *mamash* external *osios*, as it explained elsewhere in this book.

blocks.text: *Malchus* of *tevuna* is still really part of the intellect, **just above the actual *osios* of the *machshava*, which is called *Leah***: the actual literal letters, like the letters in this book. As is known of the large *dalet* of *Echad*, which is *Malchus* of *tevuna* from the back of *Imma*: from there is the root of the thought coming into actual external letters.

sections.title: The intellect itself is also called thought
sections.summary: The grasped idea itself is also called thought, as one says "he's thinking": the spreading of the light of *chachma*, *chashav mah*. Deeper is the inner thought of *bina*, the depth of the concept, which never comes into letters; and so the *Zohar*'s two thoughts are the hidden thought in the will and the analytical thought that becomes *Leah*.

phrases.he: ובחינת ההשכלה עצמה המושגת בהשגה והבנה
phrases.en: And the actual *haskala atzmis* means the actual inner *sechel* of what he actually understands,

phrases.he: גם כן נקרא מחשבה
phrases.en: It's also called thought.

phrases.he: אך זהו בחינת התפשטות יש דאור החכמה
phrases.en: The spreading out of the somethingness of the light of *chachma*,

phrases.he: הנקרא חש"ב מ"ה דחכמה
phrases.en: the thinking of the *mah* of *chachma*.

blocks.text: The idea itself, grasped in understanding: **it's also called thought**, as when you say "he's thinking". Thinking does not refer only to the external letters of thought but also to the inner intellectual process of *chachma* and *bina*. This inner thinking of *bina* is the spreading of the *yesh* (somethingness) of the light of *chachma*, called *chashav mah*: **the thinking of the *mah* of *chachma***.

phrases.he: ויש בחינת פנימיות מחשבה דבינה דלא משתמע גם במחשבת שכל לבוא לכלל אותיות כלל במחשבה
והוא כמו בחינת עומק המושג, שלא נתפס גם בהשגה ומחשבה דבינה וכהאי גוונא
(ונקרא מ״י דלא קיימא לשאלה כמו שכתוב במקום אחר) ודי למבין.

blocks.text: There is an inner thought of *bina* that never comes into letters: the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept), not caught even in the grasp of *bina*. It is the intellect itself that understands the letters, not the thought or the letters. You would say it has none, but even there there are letters, and it too is called thought.

phrases.he: וזהו אית מחשבה סתימאה שברצון הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: So that's *yesh machshava, yesh machshava*, the two kinds of *machshava*: there's the hidden *machshava* in the *ratzon*,

phrases.he: ומחשבה עיונית דבינה
הבאה לכלל בחינת אותיות דמחשבה ממש, שנקרא לאה כו'
phrases.en: that comes into *mamash* letters of *machshava*, called *Leah*.

blocks.text: That is the *Zohar*'s "there is thought and there is thought": **the two kinds of *machshava***. One is the hidden thought in the will; the other is the analytical thought of *bina*, **that comes into *mamash* letters of *machshava*, called *Leah***.

sections.title: The same two thoughts in the will above the intellect
sections.summary: All this exists also in the will above the intellect: as *Arich* has a hidden *chachma*, the hidden reason of the will, so it has a hidden *bina*, a thought hidden in the hidden will. It is like the two thoughts seen openly: the will in the nerves, and the analytical thought that turns finally into letters.

phrases.he: וכל זה יש גם ברצון שלמעלה מן השכל
phrases.en: And this also exists higher than the *sechel*, all together,

phrases.he: (דהיינו בחינת בינה סתימאה דאריך אנפין, שהוא בחינת מחשבה נעלמת ברצון הנעלם, כמו שיש שכל וחכמה דאריך אנפין הנעלם מכל רעיון הנעלם, והוא בחינת חכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין הנקרא טעם כמוס לרצון כידוע,
כך יש בחינת בינה סתימאה כו')
phrases.en: The same thing, like the *chachma stima'a*, there's a *bina stima'a*.

blocks.text: **This also exists higher than the *sechel***, in the will: the *bina stima'a* (the hidden *bina*) of *Arich Anpin*, a thought hidden in the hidden will. As *Arich* has a hidden intellect and *chachma*, the *chachma stima'a*, called the *taam kamus* (the hidden reason) of the will, so **there's a *bina stima'a***.

phrases.he: והוא על דרך מה שאנו רואים ההפרש בין ב' מיני מחשבות הנזכר לעיל בגלוי
שהוא ברצון הבא בגלוי במוח, שיש רצון שבגידי המוח, שנקרא מחשבה סתימאה על שם ההעלם של זה הרצון שבמוח טרם שבא לחכמה ובינה כו'
ומחשבה עיונית, שהוא בחינת יש דאין דחכמה,
phrases.en: That's the somethingness of the *ayin* of *chachma*,

phrases.he: עד שבא לכלל אותיות דמחשבה ממש

blocks.text: This inner *bina* is like the difference seen openly between the two thoughts: the will that comes openly into the nerves of the brain, called hidden thought because that will is hidden before it comes to *chachma* and *bina*; and analytical thought, **the somethingness of the *ayin* of *chachma***, until it comes into actual letters. It is not a thought that makes anything happen; it is a thought that turns finally into letters.

sections.title: Both rooted in the soul's essence: a person thinks about what he wants
sections.summary: Both thoughts have a root in the essence of the soul, one revealed as will and one as intellect. Yet what comes up in a person's will is what comes into his thought of *bina*: he thinks about what he wants. That is how intellect comes out of will, and why *Atik*, the delight, is revealed *davka* in *bina*.

phrases.he: (ולפי הנזכר לעיל (באות ל"ח) בשרש הראשון של האותיות דמחשבה בעצם הנפש ממש,
הרי יש שרש לאותיות המחשבה דבינה גם כן בעצם הנפש
כמו שיש אורות לאותיות הרצון הבאים בגידי המוח וכהאי גוונא
רק שזה בא לבחינת גלוי לרצון,
phrases.en: this one comes revealed into a *ratzon*,

phrases.he: וזה בא לבחינת גלוי אותיות דבינה המושג בהשגת שכל
phrases.en: and this one comes revealed into an intellect.

blocks.text: By what was said in section 38 of the first root of the letters of thought in the very essence of the soul, the letters of thought of *bina* also have a root in the *etzem hanefesh* (the essence of the soul), as the letters of the will in the nerves do. Each goes all the way: one to the will in the essence of the soul, the other to the *bina* of the essence of the soul. Only, **this one comes revealed into a *ratzon*, and this one comes revealed into an intellect**.

phrases.he: ואמנם הרי אנו רואים דמה שעולה ברצונו ומחשבתו הוא אשר בא עד בחינת אותיות המחשבה דבינה,
phrases.en: But however, we see that *davka* what comes up in his *ratzon*, that's what will come into the *machshava* of *bina*.

phrases.he: שנמשך בחינת הרצון ומחשבה הנעלם במחשבה הגלויה דבינה)
phrases.en: The hidden *machshava* comes into the revealed *machshava*.

blocks.title: What he wants is what he thinks about
blocks.text: Yet **what comes up in his *ratzon*, that's what will come into the *machshava* of *bina***. What is he going to think about? *Davka* what he wants. If he wants a business, that is what he thinks about with his intellect; if he wants to be a *chassid* and learn about G-d, that is what he thinks about; a conqueror thinks how to conquer, and a man who wants to play football thinks of strategies to win the game. Though there is thought and there is thought, the thought of will is what causes the thought of *bina*. So **the hidden *machshava* comes into the revealed *machshava***, and that is what comes into reality.

blocks.question: One of the main problems people have when they start with Chassidus and Kabbalah: from the will comes chachma, and from chachma bina. What does that mean?
blocks.text: That is why the root of the intellect is said to be in *Arich*. *Bina* out of *chachma* one can see: *chachma* is a general overview of the whole thing, and *bina* a separate analysis. One can see how *middos* (emotions) come out of intellect: by your logic you figure out whether he is doing you a favor or trying to cheat you, and if it's a favor, you like him, or vice versa. But how does intellect come out of will? What he wants is what he is going to think about. A guy who wants to make money is not going to sit around thinking these things. He'll make all kinds of analyses: will the stock market go up? Should I go into this, or buy houses? With a thought of letters, he thinks about *davka* what he wants.

phrases.he: (וזהו ענין אהי״ה אשר אהי״ה דהתגלות כתר הכללי דאריך אנפין בכתר הפרטי שהוא בבינה
phrases.en: The general *Ekyeh* of the *Keser klali* gets revealed into the *Ekyeh* in the *Keser prati*, which is *bina*.

phrases.he: וכידוע ומבואר במקום אחר בענין ועבד הלוי הוא,
דהתגלות עתיק יומין בבינה דוקא
phrases.en: The revelation of the *taanug* is *davka* in *bina*.

blocks.text: That is *Ekyeh asher Ekyeh*: **the general *Ekyeh* of the *Keser klali* gets revealed into the *Ekyeh* in the *Keser prati*, which is *bina***, which is why *bina* is called a particular *Keser*. And as explained elsewhere on *v'avad haLevi hu*, *Atik Yomin* is revealed *davka* in *bina*: **the revelation of the *taanug* is *davka* in *bina***. The will follows the delight: what he has delight in is what he is going to think about.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the will called thought, and why is its thought called the hidden thought?
What are the igulim of the machshava kduma, and how does a will for a will differ from them?
If the will comes into the nerves without letters, why is the movement it makes so exact?
How does machshava iyunis work, and what do the proof from found money and the scientific method show about it?
What comes before the analytical thought, and where does that thought come from?
How does intellect come out of will?
